newsitem.title: GERMANY: German industrial output falls 1.3 pct in April.
newsitem.headline: German industrial output falls 1.3 pct in April.

text.p: German industrial output fell 1.3 percent in April from the previous month, the first decline since January, the economics ministry said on Wednesday, but it added that the April figure was likely to be revised upward.
Calculations by Reuters based on Bundesbank data show industrial output was 1.3 percent higher than in April 1996.
Output in March was up 0.3 percent from the previous month and up 3.8 percent from the year-earlier month.
"The reported monthly decline in industrial production is a real surprise," said analysts Ralf Kugelstadt and Holger Fahrinkrug of UBS in Frankfurt in a research note.
"(But) today's report does not change our perception that activity is set to accelerate in the months ahead."

Salomon Brothers analysts Gernot Nerb and Wike Groenenberg agreed, citing broader two-month comparisons. "The latest industrial production data supports the view that the economic recovery continues, particularly in manufacturing industry.
A 2.2 percent decline in manufacturing was the sole reason for the fall, while other sectors gained. Consumer goods remained particularly weak.
The UBS analysts said the predicted upward revision was unlikely to be enough to convert the April drop to a rise, but they expect April orders data to show strength.

Output in west Germany was down 1.4 percent month-on-month and up 1.1 percent year-on-year, while in east Germany output was up 2.2 percent month-on-month and up 1.7 percent from the year-earlier month.
